evidence: Cic. de Or. 2.154: nōn tulit ūllōs haec cīvitās aut glōriā clāriōrēs aut auctōritāte graviōrēs (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Tusc. 3.3: est enim glōria solida quaedam rēs et expressa, nōn adumbrāta (Lewis & Short)

terms.gloss: what adorns or does credit: an ornament, distinction, honour
evidence: Cic. Caecin. 28: decus atque ōrnāmentum jūdiciōrum (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Brut. 59: ut hominis decus ingenium, sīc ingeniī ipsīus lūmen est ēloquentia (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: A favourite word of Cicero’s in his speeches (Lewis & Short); often of a person who is the pride of his order or his city.

phrases.latin: est enim glōria solida quaedam rēs et expressa, nōn adumbrāta
phrases.english: for glory is a solid thing, clear-cut, not a mere outline

phrases.latin: ut hominis decus ingenium, sīc ingeniī ipsīus lūmen est ēloquentia
phrases.english: as a man’s glory is his mind, so the light of the mind itself is eloquence
